title: How a 1-layer transformer computes (a+b) mod 113: a sparse Fourier-frequency algorithm
label: verified (local-full, full precision)
behavior: Input [a, b, '='] with a, b in 0..112 ('=' is token 113); at the last position the model outputs (a+b) mod 113. Accuracy 1.0 on all 12769 pairs (E0002).
summary: The model represents numbers as waves (cos/sin) at a small set of frequencies mod 113: mainly 28, 17, 2 and 14, with 27 and a few minor ones. The embedding (E0003), the MLP neurons (E0011), the MLP output (E0015) and the unembedding (E0004) all use this same set. All 4 attention heads at '=' split attention ~50/50 between a and b (E0009, E0010). They act together as a mixer (only joint ablation kills the behaviour, E0006/E0008) and write almost nothing to the logits directly (E0014). mlp0 is necessary (E0007): its neurons each tune to one key frequency and write key-frequency directions that W_U reads out (E0016). The 18-dim key-frequency subspace of the operand embeddings is necessary (E0012) and sufficient (V0001: keeping only it gives 99.8% of the logit diff). On held-out data the Fourier algorithm agrees with the model on 1000/1000 inputs (V0001). All numbers are from local-full (fp32).
pseudocode:
P = 113; K = [2, 14, 17, 27, 28]            # key frequencies (E0003, E0004, E0011)
def predict(a, b):
    # 1. embed: a, b -> cos/sin(2*pi*k*x/P) for k in K       (E0003; necessary E0012, sufficient V0001)
    # 2. attention (4 heads, ~50/50 on a and b) mixes them at '='   (E0009, E0010, E0008)
    # 3. mlp0: frequency-tuned neurons combine a and b features   (E0011, E0015; necessary E0007)
    # 4. unembed reads key-frequency directions                   (E0004, E0016)
    logit = [sum(cos(2*pi*k*(a+b-c)/P) for k in K) for c in range(P)]
    return argmax(logit)                                          # = (a+b) mod P  (V0001: 1000/1000)

claims.text: The model does the task perfectly: accuracy 1.0 on all 12769 pairs, mean logit diff 72.4.
The token embedding is sparse in the Fourier basis mod 113: frequencies 28, 17, 2, 14 hold 28.5/23.1/20.0/7.2% of power (uniform would be 1.8%); 9 key frequencies hold 91.8%.
The unembedding uses the same frequencies (28/17/2/14 = 30.0/24.2/21.6/9.1%); 6 key frequencies hold 90.1% of power.
The MLP neurons cluster by frequency: k=2:190, 28:128, 17:113, 14:52, 27:19; on average 70% of a neuron's variance is on one frequency.
All 128 dims of the MLP output at '=' are periodic with best frequency in {28, 17, 2}.
From '=', each head attends ~50% to its top operand and ~0.2% to '=' itself, so attention mixes a and b ~50/50 on average.
The heads share the work: each one ablated alone removes 28-34% of the logit diff, while all 4 together reduce it to ~0.
The heads write only 1.2% of the logit diff directly; mlp0 is necessary (mean ablation leaves 1.4%).
The key-frequency subspace (18 of 128 dims) of the a and b embeddings is necessary (ablated: 0%) and sufficient (kept alone: 99.8%, 100% accuracy). A random 18-dim ablation keeps 86.4%.
The read-out goes through the 12-dim W_U key-frequency subspace: ablating it in resid_post at '=' leaves 0.2% of the logit diff.
The Fourier algorithm predict() agrees with the model on 1000/1000 held-out inputs (seed 7).

limitations: Everything was measured on local-full (fp32); there is no quantized/screening data.

Because the model is 100% accurate, 100% agreement in V0001 would hold for any correct algorithm. The exact logit form sum_k cos(w_k(a+b-c)) and the frequency weights were not fitted or measured directly.

That the MLP multiplies a and b features (product-to-sum) is inferred from the frequency structure and the roles. It was not measured directly: periodicity (E0015) does not split a-only, b-only and (a+b) terms, and the linear probe for (a+b) before vs after the MLP failed because it needs an explicit label list.
Attention numbers (E0009, E0010) are means; I did not measure how much the a/b split varies per example.
E0013 (keep-only-subspace via 'complement') silently ignored the flag and duplicated E0012. It is not used as evidence; sufficiency comes from V0001.
The DLA tool reported heads only; the MLP's direct logit share is inferred from E0007, not measured.
No component-level 'ablate everything else' test: in a 1-layer model the claimed components are the whole model.
open_questions: Does each neuron's activation depend on cos/sin(w_k(a+b)) (the joint term) rather than on a and b separately? This needs a 2-D Fourier split or a probe with explicit labels.
What does each frequency contribute? Ablate one frequency at a time to see whether any single one is enough or needed.
Why do the 4 heads share the work evenly? Do they specialise by frequency?
What role do the minor frequencies (4, 34, 43, 56) play?
